summary:
I want to tell you right away that you have my permission to turn over my Vancouver speech to your friend who is putting out the French fanzine. I trust your judgment entirely. 

As your friend Michel told you, I’ve had the flu, and Tessa was very tired then but is much more rested now. We’ve had bad money worries ... unable to pay our rent, etc., but at last some royalties came in from France, which saved our hides. God bless your country, Patrice; without it we’d both be dead (I believe the money was from a reprint by Opta, in fact). Anyhow, I’m over the flu and we both are happier now. Tess was delighted at your reaction to her story and pictures, and she says for you to keep them. It meant a lot to her to learn you’d put the one horse picture up on the wall. The other day she said to me, “If it hadn’t been for Patrice, I would have left you.” So I am grateful to you for saving our marriage, but I must admit that her remark came as a surprise to me. She feels and has always felt that in a certain real sense you were her only friend at one time. I’m glad that she feels this trust in you. Tessa has good instincts about people—very accurate. 

Today I sent back to my agent the contracts for a movie to be made of DO ANDROIDS DREAM OF ELECTRIC SHEEP? The buyer is UA, the option money is $2,000 a year, and if they go ahead then the purchase price is $25,000. We are very excited, of course. (By the way—how is UBIK coming as a screen­ play? We’re eternally excited about that too, ...
